value.zh: 為政清簡，士庶懷惠。
value.en: His administration was clear and simple, and officials and people alike were grateful.
value.literal: His government was clear and simple; gentry and commoners cherished his kindness.

value.zh: 在職數年，遷營州總管。
value.en: After several years he was transferred to commissioner-general of Ying.
value.literal: After several years in office he was transferred to Commissioner-General of Ying.

value.zh: 藝容貌瑰偉，每夷狄參謁，必整儀衛，盛服以見之，獨坐滿一榻。
value.en: Yi was striking in appearance; whenever frontier peoples came to audience he arrayed full guard of honor and splendid dress, sitting alone across an entire couch.
value.literal: Yi's appearance was grand and imposing; whenever barbarians of the Yi came to audience he would always array guards of honor and wear splendid dress to receive them, sitting alone and filling a whole couch.

value.zh: 番人畏懼，莫敢仰視。
value.en: The tribesmen were awed and dared not meet his gaze.
value.literal: The barbarians feared and did not dare look up.

value.zh: 而大治產業，與北夷貿易，家資巨萬，頗為清論所譏。
value.en: Yet he amassed great estates and traded with northern tribes until his household wealth reached millions, drawing criticism from moralists.
value.literal: Yet he greatly developed estates and traded with the northern Yi; family wealth reached tens of millions, and he was rather ridiculed in pure discussion.

value.zh: 開皇十五年卒官，時年五十八。
value.en: In Kaihuang year fifteen he died in office at fifty-eight.
value.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang he died in office, aged fifty-eight.

value.zh: 諡曰懷。
value.en: His posthumous name was Huai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Huai.

value.zh: 藝弟沖沖字世沖，少以名家子，在周釋褐衛公府禮曹參軍。
value.en: Yi's younger brother Chong, styled Shichong, entered office under the Zhou as ritual officer in the household of the Duke of Wei.
value.literal: Yi's younger brother Chong—Chong styled Shichong—in youth as a son of a famous house, upon leaving the sackcloth under Zhou became Army Ritual Officer of the Duke of Wei's household.

value.zh: 後從大將軍元定渡江伐陳，為陳人所虜，周武帝以幣贖而還之。
value.en: He later followed Yuan Ding across the Yangzi against Chen, was captured, and was ransomed back by Zhou Emperor Wu.
value.literal: Later he followed Grand General Yuan Ding in crossing the river to attack Chen and was captured by the Chen; Emperor Wu of Zhou redeemed him with treasure and returned him.

value.zh: 帝複令沖以馬千匹使于陳，以贖開府賀拔華等五十人及元定之柩而還。
value.en: The emperor sent him to Chen with a thousand horses to ransom fifty captives including Heba Hua and recover Yuan Ding's coffin.
value.literal: The emperor again ordered Chong to go to Chen with a thousand horses as envoy, to redeem fifty men including Pillar of State Heba Hua and Yuan Ding's coffin and return.

value.zh: 沖有辭辯，奉使稱旨，累遷少禦伯下大夫，加上儀同。
value.en: Eloquent as an envoy, he rose to lower imperial bearer grand master with the added rank of upper pillar of state.
value.literal: Chong had eloquence in debate; as envoy he answered the purpose and was repeatedly promoted to Lower Imperial Bearer Grand Master, with Upper Pillar of State added.

value.zh: 于時稽胡屢為寇亂，沖自請安集之，因拜汾州刺史。
value.en: When the Jiéhu raided repeatedly he volunteered to pacify them and was made prefect of Fen.
value.literal: At that time the Jiéhu repeatedly made raids and disturbances; Chong himself requested to pacify them and was appointed Prefect of Fen.

value.zh: 高祖踐阼，征為兼散騎常侍，進位開府，賜爵安固縣侯。
value.en: At Gaozu's accession he was summoned as concurrent regular attendant, made pillar of state, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu.
value.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned as Concurrent Regular Attendant, advanced to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu.

value.zh: 歲餘，發南汾州胡千餘人北築長城，在途皆亡。
value.en: A year later more than a thousand southern Fenzhou Hu sent north to build the Great Wall deserted on the march.
value.literal: After more than a year, over a thousand men of the southern Fenzhou Hu were sent north to build the Long Wall, and on the road all fled.

value.zh: 上呼沖問計，沖曰：「夷狄之性，易為反覆，皆由牧宰不稱之所致也。
value.en: The emperor asked his counsel; Chong said, "Barbarians are quick to turn treacherous when their overseers are unfit.
value.literal: The emperor called Chong to ask his plan; Chong said: "The nature of the Yi and Di is easy to turn back and forth—all is caused by pastoral officials not fitting their posts.

value.zh: 臣請以理綏靜，可不勞兵而定。」
value.en: I can pacify them by just governance without troops."
value.literal: Your servant requests to soothe them with reason; without troubling the army it can be settled."

value.zh: 上然之，因命沖綏懷叛者。
value.en: The emperor agreed and sent Chong to win over the deserters.
value.literal: The emperor approved and ordered Chong to soothe and cherish the rebels.

value.zh: 月餘皆至，並赴長城，上下書勞勉之。
value.en: Within a month all returned and went to the wall; the court praised them in edicts.
value.literal: Within a month all arrived and all went to the Long Wall; edicts from above and below praised and encouraged them.

value.zh: 尋拜石州刺史，甚得諸胡歡心。
value.en: He was soon made prefect of Shi and won the frontier peoples' loyalty.
value.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Shi and greatly won the hearts of the various Hu.

value.zh: 以母憂去職。
value.en: He resigned to mourn his mother.
value.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.

value.zh: 俄而起為南寧州總管，持節撫慰。
value.en: He was soon recalled as commissioner-general of Nanning with credentials to pacify the south.
value.literal: Shortly he was recalled as Commissioner-General of Nanning, holding credentials to comfort and soothe.

value.zh: 複遣柱國王長述以兵繼進。
value.en: Pillar of State Wang Changshu was sent with troops in support.
value.literal: Again Pillar of State Wang Changshu was sent with troops to follow in support.

value.zh: 沖上表固讓。
value.en: Chong petitioned firmly to decline.
value.literal: Chong memorialized firmly declining.

value.zh: 詔曰：「西南夷裔，屢有生梗，每相殘賊，朕甚湣之，已命戎徒，清撫邊服。
value.en: An edict read: "Southwestern tribes repeatedly rebel and slaughter one another; We pity them and have sent troops to pacify the frontier.
value.literal: An edict said: "The Yi tribes of the southwest repeatedly show obstinacy; they constantly slaughter one another, and We greatly pity them. We have already ordered warriors to clear and soothe the border regions.

value.zh: 以開府器幹堪濟，識略英遠，軍旅事重，故以相任。
value.en: Your capacity and insight suit military command, and We therefore entrust this mission to you.
value.literal: Because as Pillar of State your capacity and ability can cross difficulties, your insight and strategy are heroic and far-reaching, and military affairs are weighty, We therefore entrust you.

value.zh: 知在艱疚，日月未多，金革奪情，蓋有通式。
value.en: Though your mourning is recent, custom allows service to resume in wartime.
value.literal: Knowing you are in the hardship of mourning and the days and months are not many, the metal and leather seizing feeling—there is a general rule.

value.zh: 宜自抑割，即膺往旨。」
value.en: Restrain your grief and obey this order at once."
value.literal: You should yourself restrain and cut short, and immediately receive the former decree."

value.zh: 沖既至南寧，渠帥爨震及西爨首領皆詣府參謁。
value.en: At Nanning the chieftains Cuan Zhen and the western Cuan leaders all came to his headquarters.
value.literal: When Chong reached Nanning, chieftain Cuan Zhen and the western Cuan leaders all came to the headquarters to pay respects.

value.zh: 上大悅，下詔褒揚之。
value.en: The emperor was delighted and issued a commendatory edict.
value.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict praising him.

value.zh: 其兄子伯仁，隨沖在府，掠人之妻，士卒縱暴，邊人失望。
value.en: His nephew Boren, serving on his staff, seized women and soldiers plundered until the frontier lost faith.
value.literal: His elder brother's son Boren followed Chong at the headquarters, seized people's wives, and soldiers indulged in violence—the border people lost hope.

value.zh: 上聞而大怒，令蜀王秀治其事。
value.en: The emperor was furious and ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to investigate.
value.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly angry and ordered Prince of Shu Xiu to investigate the matter.

value.zh: 益州長史元岩，性方正，案沖無所寬貸，沖竟坐免。
value.en: Yi region chief administrator Yuan Yan investigated without favor and Chong was dismissed.
value.literal: Chief Administrator of Yi Region Yuan Yan by nature was upright and square; investigating Chong he showed no indulgence, and Chong in the end was dismissed for the offense.

value.zh: 其弟太子洗馬世約，譖岩于皇太子。
value.en: His brother Shiyue, crown prince libationer, slandered Yan to the heir apparent.
value.literal: His younger brother the Crown Prince's Libationer Shiyue slandered Yan to the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 上謂太子曰：「古人有沽酒酸而不售者，為噬犬耳。
value.en: The emperor told the crown prince, "The ancients had a wine seller whose stock turned sour because of a biting dog.
value.literal: The emperor told the Crown Prince: "The ancients had one whose wine turned sour and would not sell—because of a biting dog.

value.zh: 今何用世約乎？
value.en: What use is Shiyue to you now?
value.literal: Now what use is Shiyue?

value.zh: 適累汝也。」
value.en: He will only burden you."
value.literal: He will only burden you."

value.zh: 世約遂除名。
value.en: Shiyue was struck from the registers.
value.literal: Shiyue was thereupon removed from the rolls.

value.zh: 後數載，令沖檢校括州事。
value.en: Years later Chong was ordered to inspect Kuozhou.
value.literal: Several years later Chong was ordered to inspect and manage Kuozhou affairs.

value.zh: 時東陽賊帥陶子定、吳州賊帥羅慧方並聚眾為亂，攻圍婺州永康、烏程諸縣，沖率兵擊破之。
value.en: Rebel leaders Tao Ziding and Luo Huifang besieged Wuzhou counties; Chong routed them.
value.literal: At that time the bandit chieftain Tao Ziding of Dongyang and the bandit chieftain Luo Huifang of Wu Region both gathered crowds in rebellion, attacking and besieging Yongkang of Wuzhou and Wucheng and other counties; Chong led troops and defeated them.

value.zh: 改封義豐縣候，檢校泉州事。
value.en: He was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yifeng and made inspector of Quanzhou.
value.literal: He changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Yifeng and was made inspector of Quanzhou affairs.

value.zh: 尋拜營州總管。
value.en: He was soon made commissioner-general of Ying again.
value.literal: Soon he was appointed Commissioner-General of Ying.

value.zh: 沖容貌都雅，寬厚得眾心。
value.en: Refined in bearing and generous in manner, he won popular loyalty.
value.literal: Chong's appearance was refined and elegant; generous and thick, he won the people's hearts.

value.zh: 懷撫靺鞨、契丹，皆能致其死力。
value.en: He soothed the Mohe and Khitan until they would fight to the death for him.
value.literal: Comforting and soothing the Mohe and Khitan, he could all bring them to devote their utmost strength.

value.zh: 奚、霫畏懼，朝貢相續。
value.en: The Xi and Xie tribes submitted and sent tribute in succession.
value.literal: The Xi and Xie feared and were in awe; tribute and missions followed in succession.

value.zh: 高麗嘗入寇，沖率兵擊走之。
value.en: When Goguryeo raided he drove them back by force.
value.literal: Goguryeo once entered in raid; Chong led troops and struck and drove them off.

value.zh: 仁壽中，高祖為豫章王暕納沖女為妃，征拜民部尚書。
value.en: In Renshou, Gaozu betrothed Chong's daughter to Prince Yang Guang and made him minister of the people.
value.literal: In Renshou, Gaozu for Prince of Yuzhang Yang Guang took Chong's daughter as consort and summoned him as Minister of the People.

value.zh: 未幾，卒，時年六十六。
value.en: He died soon afterward at sixty-six.
value.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-six.

value.zh: 少子挺，最知名。
value.en: His youngest son Ting was the most famous.
value.literal: His youngest son Ting was most renowned.

value.zh: 從父弟壽壽字世齡。
value.en: His paternal cousin Shou, styled Shiling.
value.literal: Paternal cousin Shou—Shou styled Shiling.

value.zh: 父孝寬，周上柱國、鄖國公。
value.en: His father Xiaokuan was Zhou upper pillar of state and Duke of Yun.
value.literal: Father Xiaokuan was Zhou Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Yun.

value.zh: 壽在周，以貴公子，早有令譽，為右侍上士，遷千牛備身。
value.en: Under the Zhou the young noble Shou won early renown as right attendant upper gentleman and thousand-ox guard.
value.literal: Shou in Zhou, as a son of an honored house, early had fine reputation, was Right Attendant Upper Gentleman, and transferred to Thousand-Ox Guard.

value.zh: 趙王為雍州牧，引為主簿。
value.en: When Prince Zhao became prefect of Yong he made Shou his chief clerk.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao was Prefect of Yong Region he drew him as Chief Clerk.

value.zh: 尋遷少禦伯。
value.en: He was soon promoted to lower imperial bearer.
value.literal: Soon he transferred to Lower Imperial Bearer.

value.zh: 武帝親征高氏，拜京兆尹，委以後事。
value.en: When Emperor Wu campaigned against the Gao he made Shou metropolitan governor of Jingzhao with charge of the rear.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu personally campaigned against the Gao clan he appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and entrusted him with rear affairs.

value.zh: 以父軍功，賜爵永安縣侯，邑八百戶。
value.en: For his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with eight hundred households.
value.literal: Because of his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with a fief of eight hundred households.

value.zh: 高祖為丞相，以其父平尉迥，拜夀儀同三司，進封滑國公，邑五千戶。
value.en: When Gaozu was chancellor he made Shou pillar of state, third rank, then Duke of Hua with five thousand households for pacifying Jiong.
value.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, because his father pacified Yuwen Jiong he appointed Shou Pillar of State, Third Rank, advanced to Duke of Hua with a fief of five thousand households.

value.zh: 俄以父喪去職。
value.en: He soon resigned to mourn his father.
value.literal: Shortly he left office on mourning for his father.

value.zh: 高祖愛禪，起令視事，尋遷恆、毛二州刺史，頗有治名。
value.en: At the founding of Sui he was recalled to duty, then governed Heng and Mao with distinction.
value.literal: When Gaozu received the love of abdication he recalled him and ordered him to resume duties; soon he transferred to Prefect of Heng and Mao—in both he had reputation for good governance.

value.zh: 開皇十年，以疾征還，卒于家，時年四十二。
value.en: In Kaihuang year ten he was recalled ill and died at home at forty-two.
value.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang, because of illness he was summoned back and died at home, aged forty-two.

value.zh: 諡曰定。
value.en: His posthumous name was Ding.
value.literal: Posthumous title Ding.

value.zh: 仁壽中，高祖為晉王昭納其女為妃。
value.en: In Renshou Gaozu betrothed his daughter to Prince Yang Zhao of Jin.
value.literal: In Renshou, Gaozu for Prince of Jin Yang Zhao took his daughter as consort.

value.zh: 以其子保巒嗣。
value.en: His son Baoluan succeeded him.
value.literal: His son Baoluan succeeded.

value.zh: 世康從父弟操，字元節，剛簡有風概。
value.en: Shikang's paternal cousin Cao, styled Yuanjie, was stern, principled, and imposing.
value.literal: Shikang's paternal cousin Cao, styled Yuanjie, was firm and simple with spirit and bearing.

value.zh: 仕周，致位上開府、光州刺史。
value.en: Under the Zhou he rose to upper pillar of state and prefect of Guang.
value.literal: Serving Zhou, he reached Upper Pillar of State and Prefect of Guang.

value.zh: 高祖為丞相，以平尉迥功，進位柱國，封平桑郡公，曆青、荊二州總管，卒官。
value.en: When Gaozu was chancellor he was made pillar of state and Duke of Pingsang for pacifying Jiong, then commissioner-general of Qing and Jing until he died in office.
value.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, for merit in pacifying Yuwen Jiong he advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingsang, and served in succession as Commissioner-General of Qing and Jing—he died in office.

value.zh: 諡曰靜。
value.en: His posthumous name was Jing.
value.literal: Posthumous title Jing.

value.zh: 柳機，字匡時，河東解人也。
value.en: Liu Ji, styled Kuangshi, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
value.literal: Liu Ji—Ji styled Kuangshi—was a native of Jie in Hedong.

value.zh: 父慶，魏尚書左僕射。
value.en: His father Qing was left vice director of the secretariat under the Wei.
value.literal: Father Qing was Wei Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 機偉儀容，有器局，頗涉經史。
value.en: Ji had imposing presence and breadth of vision and was well read in the classics and histories.
value.literal: Ji had grand bearing and capacity, and was quite versed in the classics and histories.

value.zh: 年十九，周武帝時為魯公，引為記室。
value.en: At nineteen, when Zhou Emperor Wu was still Duke of Lu, Ji became his recorder.
value.literal: At age nineteen, in the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou when he was Duke of Lu, he was drawn as Recorder.

value.zh: 及帝嗣位，自宣納上士累遷少納言、太子宮尹，封平齊縣公。
value.en: When the emperor succeeded he rose from secretariat gentleman to lower chamberlain and palace chamberlain of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi.
value.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the throne, from Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat he was promoted in succession to Lower Chamberlain and Palace Chamberlain of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi.

value.zh: 從帝平齊，拜開府，轉司宗中大夫。
value.en: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was made pillar of state, then grand master of the imperial clan.
value.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi he was appointed Pillar of State and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of the Imperial Clan.

value.zh: 宣帝時，遷禦正上大夫。
value.en: Under Emperor Xuan he became upper grand master of imperial rectification.
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he transferred to Upper Grand Master of the Imperial Rectification.

value.zh: 機見帝失德，屢諫不聽，恐禍及己，托于鄭譯，陰求出外，於是拜華州刺史。
value.en: Seeing the emperor's debauchery and failing to reform him, Ji feared for his life, relied on Zheng Yi, and secured appointment as prefect of Hua.
value.literal: Ji saw the emperor's loss of virtue and repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded; fearing disaster would reach himself, he entrusted himself to Zheng Yi and secretly sought to go outside, and was thereupon appointed Prefect of Hua.

value.zh: 及高祖作相，征還京師。
value.en: When Gaozu became chancellor he was recalled to the capital.
value.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was summoned back to the capital.

value.zh: 時周代舊臣皆勸禪讓，機獨義形於色，無所陳請。
value.en: When Zhou ministers urged abdication Ji alone showed open disapproval and made no petition.
value.literal: At that time the old ministers of the Zhou all urged abdication; Ji alone showed righteousness in his countenance and made no memorial request.

value.zh: 俄拜衛州刺史。
value.en: He was soon made prefect of Wei.
value.literal: Shortly he was appointed Prefect of Wei.

value.zh: 及踐阼，進爵建安郡公，邑二千四百戶，征為納言。
value.en: At the founding of Sui he was raised to Duke of Jian'an with twenty-four hundred households and made chamberlain.
value.literal: When he ascended the throne he advanced in noble rank to Duke of Jian'an with a fief of twenty-four hundred households and was summoned as Chamberlain.

value.zh: 機性寬簡，有雅望，然當近侍，無所損益，又好飲酒，不親細務，在職數年，複出為華州刺史。
value.en: Though refined and respected, he drank heavily, neglected detail, and after years at court returned to Hua as prefect.
value.literal: Ji by nature was generous and simple, with refined standing, yet while serving in close attendance he made no additions or subtractions; he also loved drinking wine and did not attend to fine affairs—in office several years he again went out as Prefect of Hua.

value.zh: 奉詔每月朝見。
value.en: He was ordered to attend court monthly.
value.literal: He received an edict to attend court monthly.

value.zh: 尋轉冀州刺史。
value.en: He was soon transferred to prefect of Ji.
value.literal: Soon he transferred to Prefect of Ji.

value.zh: 後征入朝，以其子述尚蘭陵公主，禮遇益隆。
value.en: Recalled to court, he gained favor when his son Shu married Princess Lanling.
value.literal: Later he was summoned to court; because his son Shu married Princess Lanling, favor and treatment grew richer.

value.zh: 任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。
value.en: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was only five when Gongzong died, yet he wailed without stopping.
value.literal: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was five years old when Gongzong died, and he wailed without cease.

value.zh: 世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！」
value.en: Shizu heard and called for him, took him in his arms, and wept. "How is it that you already have a grown man's heart?"
value.literal: Shizu heard of this, summoned him, embraced him, and wept, saying, "What do you know, to have the mind of a grown man?"

value.zh: 和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。
value.en: In Heping year 5 he received his fief and was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and commander of Helong Garrison.
value.literal: In Heping year 5 he was enfeoffed and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and grand commander of Helong Garrison.

value.zh: 顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。
value.en: Under Xianzu he commanded the armies inside and outside the court, served as seated high minister of the central capital, heard civil suits, and won wide renown.
value.literal: Under Xianzu he was appointed commander of all military affairs within and beyond the court and seated high minister of the central capital; he heard civil lawsuits and won great praise in his time.

value.zh: 延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。
value.en: During the Yanxing era, Xianzu gathered his ministers, intending to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.
value.literal: During Yanxing, Xianzu assembled the officials and wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.

value.zh: 王公卿士，莫敢先言。
value.en: Among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers, no one dared speak first.
value.literal: None among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers dared speak first.

value.zh: 雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。
value.en: Yun stepped forward. "Your Majesty is raising an age of peace and shelters all within the four seas. How could you turn away from the ancestral temples above and cast off the people below?
value.literal: Yun stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty is now exalting great peace and overseeing all within the four seas; how could you above violate the ancestral temples and below abandon the myriad people?

value.zh: 父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。
value.en: Father-to-son succession has long been the rule; since imperial Wei arose, it has never been altered.
value.literal: The succession from father to son has come down for a long time; since the rise of imperial Wei, it has not been changed.

value.zh: 皇儲正統，聖德夙章。
value.en: The crown prince is the rightful heir, and his virtue has shone since early youth.
value.literal: The crown prince is the orthodox heir, and his sagely virtue was manifest early.

value.zh: 陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。
value.en: If Your Majesty truly wishes to lay aside worldly affairs and nourish your spirit in quiet freedom, the throne should pass to the heir. If you set the heir aside and lightly move the imperial pivot, I fear this defies the former sages and will shock the hearts of men.
value.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to cut away worldly affairs and nourish the spirit in clear freedom, the charge of the heir should continue the precious calendar; if you mean to set aside the heir and lightly shift the imperial pivot, I fear it is not the intention of the former sages and will alarm human feeling.

value.zh: 又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。」
value.en: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors. If Your Majesty suddenly changes the sacred vessel, you will offend the ancestral spirits above and open the way to treachery and disorder below. Fortune and disaster begin here; please think deeply and proceed with care."
value.literal: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors, yet Your Majesty would suddenly change the sacred vessel, above going against the seven temples and seven spirits and below lengthening the road of treachery and disorder. This is where fortune and disaster begin; I beg you to think deeply and act carefully."

value.zh: 太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。」
value.en: Grand Marshal Yuan He also spoke. "If Your Majesty chooses from among the princes and abdicates to an imperial uncle, I fear the order of the ancestral rites will be thrown into confusion, and later ages will condemn the offerings as improper. I beg you to weigh Rencheng's words."
value.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan He also stepped forward and said, "If Your Majesty now wishes to choose externally among the princes and abdicate to an imperial uncle, I fear that in spring and autumn sacrifices the order of Zhao and Mu will be confused, and after ten thousand generations there will surely be criticism of improper offerings. I earnestly hope you will consider Rencheng's words."

value.zh: 東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。
value.en: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others added, "Although the crown prince's virtue is already clear, he is still very young.
value.literal: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others advanced and said, "Though the crown prince's sagely virtue has long been evident, he is in truth still young.

value.zh: 陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！」
value.en: Your Majesty is young and has only begun to govern; all under heaven look to you, and every land waits on your heart. If you prize private purity and give no thought to the world, what becomes of the ancestral temples? What becomes of the people?"
value.literal: Your Majesty is rich in years and has only begun to oversee the mechanisms of government; all under heaven look up to you, and the whole land waits with longing. If you wish to exalt solitary goodness and give no thought to the myriad things, what of the ancestral temples? What of the millions of people?"

value.zh: 顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。」
value.en: Xianzu replied, "The crown prince is the rightful line, receiving the succession from Wenzu. With all of you to assist him, what could be wrong?"
value.literal: Xianzu said, "The heir's palace is the orthodox line; he received the completion from Wenzu. If all you gentlemen assist him, what is unacceptable?"

value.zh: 於是傳位於高祖。
value.en: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.
value.literal: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.

value.zh: 後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。
value.en: Later, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Yun served as grand commander of the central army and followed Xianzu against them, meeting them in the great desert.
value.literal: Later, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Yun became grand commander of the central army, followed Xianzu in campaigning against them, and met them in the great desert.

value.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。
value.en: The affair is recorded in the Rouran biography.
value.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the Rouran biography.

value.zh: 後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。
value.en: Later, when the Qiuchi Di rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and put them down.
value.literal: Later, when the Di of Qiuchi rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and suppressed them.

value.zh: 除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。
value.en: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province.
value.literal: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, with an opened office, and Inspector of Xu Province.

value.zh: 雲以太妃蓋氏薨，表求解任，顯祖不許，雲悲號動疾，乃許之。
value.en: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he asked to resign. Xianzu refused, but Yun grieved and wailed until he fell ill, and only then was he allowed to step down.
value.literal: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he memorialized requesting release from office. Xianzu refused; Yun's grief and wailing brought on illness, and only then was he permitted.

value.zh: 性善撫綏，得徐方之心，為百姓所追戀。
value.en: He was naturally good at soothing and governing people, won the hearts of Xu, and was remembered fondly by its people.
value.literal: By nature he was good at comforting and pacifying people, won the hearts of the Xu region, and was long remembered by the commoners.

value.zh: 送遺錢貨，一無所受。
value.en: He refused every gift of money or goods sent to him.
value.literal: Of the money and goods sent to him as gifts, he accepted not a single thing.

value.zh: 顯祖聞而嘉之。
value.en: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.
value.literal: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.

value.zh: 復拜侍中、中都大官，賜帛千匹、羊千口。
value.en: He was again made Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and received a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.
value.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and was granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.

value.zh: 出為冀州刺史，仍本將軍。
value.en: He was sent out as inspector of Ji Province, retaining his former general's rank.
value.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province, retaining his original generalship.

value.zh: 雲留心政事，甚得下情，於是合州請戶輸絹五尺、粟五升以報雲恩。
value.en: Yun governed attentively and understood those under him so well that the whole province asked to give five chi of silk and five sheng of grain per household in gratitude for his kindness.
value.literal: Yun gave close attention to government and greatly won the feelings of those below; thereupon the whole province requested that each household contribute five chi of silk and five sheng of grain to repay Yun's kindness.

value.zh: 高祖嘉之，遷使持節、都督陝西諸軍事、征南大將軍、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。
value.en: Gaozu praised him and transferred him to serve as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, commander of Chang'an Garrison, and inspector of Yong Province.
value.literal: Gaozu praised him and transferred him as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, grand commander of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yong Province.

value.zh: 雲廉謹自修，留心庶獄，挫抑豪強，羣盜息止，州民頌之者千有餘人。
value.en: Yun was upright and careful, gave close attention to common lawsuits, checked the powerful, and brought banditry to an end; more than a thousand people in the province praised him in verse.
value.literal: Yun cultivated himself in integrity and caution, attended carefully to ordinary lawsuits, suppressed the powerful and arrogant, and bandits ceased; more than a thousand people of the province sang his praises.

value.zh: 文明太后嘉之，賜帛千匹。
value.en: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and gave him a thousand bolts of silk.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and granted him a thousand bolts of silk.

value.zh: 太和五年，薨於州。
value.en: In Taihe year 5 he died in office in the province.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he died in the province.

value.zh: 遺令薄葬，勿受賵禭。
value.en: In his last instructions he ordered a simple burial and forbade the acceptance of funerary gifts.
value.literal: His final instructions ordered a modest burial and forbade acceptance of funerary gifts.

value.zh: 諸子奉遵其旨。
value.en: His sons carried out his wishes.
value.literal: His sons respectfully followed his wishes.

value.zh: 喪至京師，車駕親臨，哭之哀慟，贈以本官，諡曰康。
value.en: When his coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person and wept bitterly over him; Yun was posthumously restored to his offices and titled Kang.
value.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person, wept over him with deep grief, posthumously granted him his former offices, and gave him the title Kang.

value.zh: 陪葬雲中之金陵。
value.en: He was buried alongside the Jinling mausoleum at Yunzhong.
value.literal: He was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.

value.zh: 雲長子澄，字道鎮，少而好學。
value.en: Yun's eldest son Cheng, styled Daozhen, loved learning from an early age.
value.literal: Yun's eldest son Cheng, courtesy name Daozhen, loved learning from youth.

value.zh: 及康王薨，澄居喪以孝聞。
value.en: After Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial devotion in mourning.
value.literal: When Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial conduct during mourning.

value.zh: 襲封，加征北大將軍。
value.en: He inherited the fief and was given the added rank Grand General Who Conquers the North.
value.literal: He inherited the fief and was additionally made Grand General Who Conquers the North.

value.zh: 高祖時，蠕蠕犯塞，加澄使持節、都督北討諸軍事以討之。
value.en: Under Gaozu, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Cheng was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the northern expedition against them.
value.literal: In Gaozu's time, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Cheng was added as Bearer of the Staff and commander of the armies for the northern campaign to attack them.

value.zh: 蠕蠕遁走，又以氐羌反叛，除都督梁益荊三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、梁州刺史。
value.en: The Rouran fled. Later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and inspector of Liang Province.
value.literal: The Rouran fled; later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Liang Province.

value.zh: 文明太后引見澄，誡厲之，顧謂中書令李沖曰：「此兒風神吐發，德音閑婉，當為宗室領袖。
value.en: Empress Dowager Wenming received Cheng, admonished him, then turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong. "This young man's bearing is splendid and his speech is gentle; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned Cheng, admonished him, and turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong, saying, "This child's bearing and expression are outstanding, and his words are gentle and refined; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.

value.zh: 是行使之必稱我意。
value.en: On this mission he will surely satisfy me.
value.literal: On this mission he will certainly satisfy my intent.

value.zh: 卿但記之，我不妄談人物也。」
value.en: Remember this: I do not misjudge men."
value.literal: You need only remember this; I do not speak of men falsely."

value.zh: 梁州氐帥楊仲顯、婆羅、楊卜兄弟及符叱盤等，自以居邊地險，世為山狡。
value.en: The Di leaders in Liang Province, including Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, and Fu Chipan, trusted in the rugged frontier and had long lived as mountain raiders.
value.literal: The Di leaders of Liang Province, Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, Fu Chipan, and others relied on living in dangerous borderlands and had for generations acted as mountain brigands.

value.zh: 澄至州，量彼風俗，誘導懷附。
value.en: When Cheng arrived, he studied their customs and coaxed them into allegiance.
value.literal: When Cheng reached the province, he assessed their customs and guided them into submission.

value.zh: 表送婆羅，授仲顯循城鎮副將，楊卜廣業太守，叱盤固道鎮副將，自餘首帥，各隨才而用之，款附者賞，違命加誅，於是仇池帖然，西南款順。
value.en: He sent Poluo to court, made Zhongxian deputy commander at Xuncheng, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander at Gudao, and used the other chiefs according to their abilities. Those who submitted were rewarded, those who resisted were punished; Qiuchi was pacified and the southwest came over.
value.literal: He memorialized to send Poluo to court, appointed Zhongxian deputy commander of Xuncheng Garrison, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander of Gudao Garrison; the remaining chiefs were each employed according to their talents. Those who sincerely submitted were rewarded, and those who disobeyed were punished. Thus Qiuchi became settled, and the southwest submitted.

value.zh: 加侍中，賜衣一襲、乘馬一匹，以旌其能。
value.en: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and given a set of robes and a riding horse in recognition of his skill.
value.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and was granted one set of robes and one riding horse to commend his ability.

value.zh: 後轉征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史，甚有聲績。
value.en: Later he became Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province, earning a strong record of achievement.
value.literal: Later he was transferred as Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as Inspector of Xu Province, where he had a very strong reputation for achievement.

value.zh: 朝於京師，引見於皇信堂。
value.en: He came to the capital for court audience and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.
value.literal: He came to court at the capital and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.

value.zh: 高祖詔澄曰：「昔鄭子產鑄刑書，而晉叔向非之。
value.en: Gaozu asked Cheng, "When Zheng Zichan cast the penal code, Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.
value.literal: Gaozu issued an edict to Cheng: "In former times Zheng Zichan cast the written laws, and Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.

value.zh: 此二人皆是賢士，得失竟誰？」
value.en: Both were worthy men; in the end, who was right?"
value.literal: Both men were worthies; in the end, who was right and who was wrong?"

value.zh: 對曰：「鄭國寡弱，攝於強鄰，民情去就，非刑莫制，故鑄刑書以示威。
value.en: Cheng replied, "Zheng was weak and hemmed in by powerful neighbors. The people could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the laws to show authority.
value.literal: Cheng replied, "The state of Zheng was weak and constrained by powerful neighbors; the people's movements could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the written laws to display authority.

value.zh: 雖乖古式，合今權道，隨時濟世，子產為得。
value.en: Though it violated ancient form, it fit the needs of the moment. Zichan adapted to his age and helped the world, so he was right.
value.literal: Though this departed from ancient norms, it suited the expedient way of that time; he adapted to the age and aided the world, so Zichan was right.

value.zh: 而叔向譏議，示不忘古，可與論道，未可語權。」
value.en: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he had not forgotten antiquity; one could discuss principle with him, but not expedience."
value.literal: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he did not forget antiquity; one may discuss the Way with him, but not expediency."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「任城當欲為魏之子產也。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be Wei's Zichan."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be the Wei state's Zichan."

value.zh: 澄曰：「子產道合當時，聲流竹素。
value.en: Cheng replied, "Zichan's way suited his time, and his name passed into the histories.
value.literal: Cheng said, "Zichan's way matched his time, and his name was handed down in the bamboo and silk records.

value.zh: 臣既庸近，何敢庶幾。
value.en: I am mediocre and shallow. How could I dare compare myself to him?
value.literal: Your servant is mediocre and shallow; how would I dare hope to approach him?

value.zh: 今陛下以四海為家，宣文德以懷天下，但江外尚阻，車書未一，季世之民，易以威伏，難以禮治。
value.en: Your Majesty now makes the four seas your household and uses civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river resistance remains, and script and carriage tracks are not yet one. People in a late age are easy to subdue by force and hard to govern by ritual.
value.literal: Now Your Majesty has made the four seas your household and proclaims civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river there is still obstruction, and carriage tracks and writing have not yet been unified. People of a declining age are easy to subdue with authority and hard to govern by ritual.

value.zh: 愚謂子產之法，猶應暫用，大同之後，便以道化之。」
value.en: In my foolish view, Zichan's methods should still be used for a time; once unity is complete, then the Way can transform them."
value.literal: In my foolish view, Zichan's laws should still be used for a time; after great unity is achieved, then they may be transformed by the Way."

value.zh: 高祖心方革變，深善其對，笑曰：「非任城無以識變化之體。
value.en: Gaozu was then intent on reform, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer. Smiling, he said, "Without Rencheng, no one would understand the essence of transformation.
value.literal: Gaozu's mind was then set on reform and change, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer, smiling as he said, "Without Rencheng, no one could understand the substance of transformation.

value.zh: 朕方創改朝制，當與任城共萬世之功耳。」
value.en: I am just beginning to remake the court's institutions; Rencheng and I shall share in a work for ten thousand generations."
value.literal: I am now beginning to alter the institutions of the court and shall share with Rencheng a work for ten thousand generations."

value.zh: 後徵為中書令，改授尚書令。
value.en: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and then made Director of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then reassigned as Director of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 蕭賾使庾蓽來朝，蓽見澄音韻遒雅，風儀秀逸，謂主客郎張彝曰：「往魏任城以武著稱，今魏任城乃以文見美也。」
value.en: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi found Cheng's speech forceful and elegant and his bearing refined. He told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "The former Rencheng of Wei was known for arms; this Rencheng of Wei is admired for culture."
value.literal: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi saw that Cheng's speech was strong and elegant and his bearing fine and graceful, and he told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "In the past Wei's Rencheng was known for martial prowess; now Wei's Rencheng is admired for culture."

value.zh: 時詔延四廟之子，下逮玄孫之冑，申宗宴於皇信堂，不以爵秩為列，悉序昭穆為次，用家人之禮。
value.en: At that time the court invited the imperial kin, from sons of the four temples down to great-great-grandsons, to a clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were seated not by rank but by ancestral order, using the rites of one family.
value.literal: At the time an edict extended invitation from sons of the four temples down to descendants in the dark-garment generation, holding an imperial-clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were not arranged by noble rank, but all were ordered by Zhao and Mu seniority and treated with family rites.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「行禮已畢，欲令宗室各言其志，可率賦詩。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "The rites are finished. I want each kinsman to state his aspirations; let each compose a poem."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "The rites are complete; I wish each member of the imperial clan to speak his aspirations. You may all compose poems."

value.zh: 特令澄為七言連韻，與高祖往復賭賽，遂至極歡，際夜乃罷。
value.en: He specially ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes. Cheng and Gaozu traded verses in playful contest until they were thoroughly delighted, stopping only late at night.
value.literal: He specifically ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes, and he and Gaozu exchanged verses in contest until their joy became extreme; only when night had fallen did they stop.

value.zh: 後高祖外示南討，意在謀遷，齋於明堂左个，詔太常卿王諶，親令龜卜，易筮南伐之事，其兆遇革。
value.en: Later Gaozu publicly presented plans for a southern campaign, while actually planning the capital move. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he had Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen personally divine by turtle and milfoil about the campaign; the omen was Revolution.
value.literal: Later Gaozu outwardly displayed plans for a southern campaign, but his intention was to plan the move of the capital. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he ordered Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen to divine personally by turtle shell and milfoil about the southern campaign; the sign received was Revolution.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「此是湯武革命，順天應人之卦也。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and answering the people."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, following Heaven and responding to men."

value.zh: 羣臣莫敢言。
value.en: None of the ministers dared speak.
value.literal: None of the ministers dared speak.

value.zh: 澄進曰：「易言革者更也。
value.en: Cheng stepped forward. "In the Changes, Revolution means change.
value.literal: Cheng stepped forward and said, "In the Changes, ge means change.

value.zh: 將欲應天順人，革君臣之命，湯武得之為吉。
value.en: When Tang and Wu obeyed Heaven, answered the people, and changed the mandate between ruler and minister, this hexagram was auspicious.
value.literal: When one is about to accord with Heaven and respond to men and change the mandate between ruler and minister, Tang and Wu obtained it as auspicious.

value.zh: 階下帝有天下，重光累葉。
value.en: Your Majesty already possesses the realm, with shining succession through many generations.
value.literal: Your Majesty possesses the realm, and bright succession has continued through many generations.

value.zh: 今曰卜征，乃可伐叛，不得云革命。
value.en: Today the divination is for a campaign; it may mean attacking rebels, but it cannot mean changing the mandate.
value.literal: Today you call this a divination for campaign; it can mean suppressing rebels, but it cannot be called changing the mandate.

value.zh: 此非君人之卦，未可全為吉也。」
value.en: This is not the hexagram for a reigning lord, and it cannot be taken as wholly auspicious."
value.literal: This is not a hexagram for one who rules men, and it cannot be taken wholly as auspicious."

value.zh: 高祖厲聲曰：「象云『大人虎變』，何言不吉也！」
value.en: Gaozu said sternly, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"
value.literal: Gaozu said in a stern voice, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「陛下龍興既久，豈可方同虎變！」
value.en: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long been established; how can it be compared to a tiger's change?"
value.literal: Cheng said, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long endured; how can it be compared to the tiger's change?"

value.zh: 高祖勃然作色曰：「社稷我社稷，任城而欲沮眾也！」
value.en: Gaozu's face darkened. "The state is my state. Does Rencheng mean to obstruct everyone?"
value.literal: Gaozu suddenly changed color and said, "The altars of state are my altars of state; does Rencheng wish to obstruct the assembly?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「社稷誠知陛下之社稷，然臣是社稷之臣子，豫參顧問，敢盡愚衷。」
value.en: Cheng said, "I know well that the state is Your Majesty's, but I am its servant and son. Since I have been admitted to counsel, I dare give all my foolish sincerity."
value.literal: Cheng said, "I truly know the altars of state are Your Majesty's altars, yet I am a servant and son of the state. Since I have been allowed to join in consultation, I dare exhaust my foolish sincerity."

value.zh: 高祖既銳意必行，惡澄此對，久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，亦復何傷。」
value.en: Gaozu was determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's answer, but after a long while he relented. "Each has stated his mind; what harm is there?"
value.literal: Gaozu was already determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's reply, but after a long while he relented and said, "Each has spoken his will; what harm is there?"

value.zh: 車駕還宮，便召澄，未及昇階，遙謂曰：「向者之革卦，今更欲論之。
value.en: After returning to the palace, Gaozu immediately summoned Cheng. Before Cheng had mounted the steps, Gaozu called to him from afar, "About that Revolution hexagram: I want to discuss it further.
value.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he at once summoned Cheng. Before Cheng had climbed the steps, Gaozu said to him from a distance, "That hexagram Revolution just now: I wish to discuss it further.

value.zh: 明堂之忿，懼眾人競言，阻我大計，故厲色怖文武耳，想解朕意也。」
value.en: In the Mingtang, I was angry because I feared everyone would start speaking at once and block my great plan, so I put on a stern face to frighten the civil and military officials. I trust you understood my intent."
value.literal: In the anger in the Mingtang, I feared that everyone would compete to speak and obstruct my great plan, and therefore I showed a stern face to frighten the civil and military officials. I suppose you understood my meaning."

value.zh: 乃獨謂澄曰：「今日之行，誠知不易。
value.en: Then he said to Cheng privately, "I know very well that today's undertaking is not easy.
value.literal: Then he said to Cheng alone, "Today's undertaking, I truly know, is not easy.

value.zh: 但國家興自北土，徙居平城，雖富有四海，文軌未一，此間用武之地，非可文治，移風易俗，信為甚難。
value.en: Our state rose in the north and later settled at Pingcheng. Though we possess the empire, its script and roads are not yet unified; this is a place for military power, not civil administration. Changing customs and habits here is truly difficult.
value.literal: Yet the state rose from the northern lands and moved to reside at Pingcheng. Though it possesses all within the four seas, writing and carriage tracks are not yet one; this place is ground for using arms, not one that can be governed by civil rule. To move customs and change habits is indeed very difficult.

value.zh: 崤函帝宅，河洛王里，因茲大舉，光宅中原，任城意以為何如？」
value.en: The Xiao and Han passes are an imperial seat, and the He and Luo region is a royal home. If we use this great move to establish ourselves splendidly in the Central Plain, what does Rencheng think?"
value.literal: Xiao and Han are the imperial dwelling, and the He and Luo are the royal precinct. If by this great act we brightly dwell in the Central Plain, what does Rencheng think?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「伊洛中區，均天下所據，陛下制御華夏，輯平九服，蒼生聞此，應當大慶。」
value.en: Cheng replied, "The Yi and Luo region lies at the center, the seat shared by all under Heaven. If Your Majesty governs China from there and brings peace to the nine regions, the people will surely rejoice when they hear it."
value.literal: Cheng said, "The Yi and Luo region is the central district, equally the place occupied by all under Heaven. If Your Majesty controls China and pacifies the nine regions, the common people, on hearing this, should greatly rejoice."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「北人戀本，忽聞將移，不能不驚擾也。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "The northerners cling to their homeland. If they suddenly hear that the capital is to be moved, they are bound to be alarmed and unsettled."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "The northerners are attached to their roots. If they suddenly hear that a move is planned, they cannot avoid alarm and disturbance."

value.zh: 澄曰：「此既非常之事，當非常人所知，唯須決之聖懷，此輩亦何能為也。」
value.en: Cheng replied, "This is an extraordinary matter, beyond the understanding of ordinary men. It only needs Your Majesty's decision; what can this crowd do about it?"
value.literal: Cheng said, "Since this is an extraordinary matter, it is not what ordinary people should know. It need only be decided in the sacred mind; what can this crowd do?"

value.zh: 高祖曰：「任城便是我之子房。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng is truly my Zifang."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng is indeed my Zifang."

value.zh: 加撫軍大將軍、太子少保，又兼尚書左僕射。
value.en: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while concurrently serving as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
value.literal: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and also concurrently served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

value.zh: 及駕幸洛陽，定遷都之策，高祖詔曰：「遷移之旨，必須訪眾。
value.en: When the emperor went to Luoyang and settled on moving the capital, Gaozu issued an edict: "The decision to relocate must be discussed with the officials.
value.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Luoyang and the plan to move the capital was settled, Gaozu issued an edict saying, "The purpose of relocation must be put to consultation with the multitude.

value.zh: 當遣任城馳驛向代，問彼百司，論擇可否。
value.en: Rencheng should be sent by courier to Dai to ask the officials there and discuss whether the move is acceptable.
value.literal: We should send Rencheng by relay horse toward Dai to ask the hundred offices there and deliberate on whether it should be chosen or not.

value.zh: 近日論革，今真所謂革也，王其勉之。」
value.en: Recently we discussed transformation; now this is transformation in the true sense. Let the prince exert himself."
value.literal: Recently we discussed change; now this is truly what is called change. Prince, exert yourself in this."

value.zh: 既至代都，眾聞遷詔，莫不驚駭。
value.en: When he arrived at the old capital of Dai, all who heard the relocation edict were shocked and alarmed.
value.literal: When he reached the capital at Dai, everyone who heard the edict to move the capital was shocked and frightened.

value.zh: 澄援引今古，徐以曉之，眾乃開伏。
value.en: Cheng cited examples from antiquity and recent times, explaining the matter patiently, and only then did everyone understand and accept it.
value.literal: Cheng cited past and present and gradually explained it to them, and only then did all understand and submit.

value.zh: 澄遂南馳還報，會車駕於滑臺。
value.en: Cheng then hurried south to report back, meeting the emperor at Huatai.
value.literal: Cheng then hastened south to report back and met the imperial carriage at Huatai.

value.zh: 高祖大悅曰：「若非任城，朕事業不得就也。」
value.en: Gaozu was delighted. "Without Rencheng, my undertaking could not have succeeded."
value.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "If not for Rencheng, my undertaking could not have been accomplished."

value.zh: 從幸鄴宮，除吏部尚書。
value.en: He accompanied the emperor to Ye Palace and was appointed Minister of Personnel.
value.literal: He followed the emperor to Ye Palace and was appointed Minister of Personnel.

value.zh: 及幸代，車駕北巡，留澄銓簡舊臣。
value.en: When the emperor went to Dai and toured the north, Cheng was left to review and rank the old officials.
value.literal: When the emperor went to Dai and the imperial carriage made a northern tour, Cheng was left behind to select and rank the former officials.

value.zh: 初，魏自公侯以下，迄于選臣，動有萬數，冗散無事。
value.en: At that time in Wei, from dukes and marquises down to appointed officials, there were often tens of thousands of supernumerary men, idle and without duties.
value.literal: At first, in Wei, from dukes and marquises down to selected officials, there were often tens of thousands, redundant and scattered, with no duties.

value.zh: 澄品為三等，量其優劣，盡其能否之用，咸無怨者。
value.en: Cheng classified them into three grades, weighed their strengths and weaknesses, and used each according to his ability; no one complained.
value.literal: Cheng graded them into three ranks, measured their merits and defects, and fully used what they could and could not do, and none resented it.

value.zh: 駕還洛京，復兼右僕射。
value.en: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, Cheng again served concurrently as Right Vice Director.
value.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the Luoyang capital, he again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.

value.zh: 高祖至北邙，遂幸洪池，命澄侍昇龍舟，因賦詩以序懷。
value.en: When Gaozu reached Beimang, he went on to Hongchi, ordered Cheng to attend him aboard the imperial boat, and composed poems there to express his thoughts.
value.literal: When Gaozu reached Beimang, he then went to Hongchi, ordered Cheng to attend him and board the dragon boat, and there composed poems to set forth his thoughts.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「朕昨夜夢一老公，頭鬢皓白，正理冠服，拜立路左。
value.en: Gaozu said, "Last night I dreamed of an old man with white hair and temples. His cap and robes were properly arranged, and he bowed as he stood on the left side of the road.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Last night I dreamed of an old man, with head and temples white, properly arranging his cap and garments, bowing and standing on the left side of the road.

value.zh: 朕怪而問之，自云晉侍中嵇紹，故此奉迎。
value.en: I was surprised and asked who he was. He said he was Xi Shao, Palace Attendant of Jin, and had come to welcome me.
value.literal: I wondered at this and asked him, and he said he was Xi Shao, Palace Attendant of Jin, and therefore had come to receive me.

value.zh: 神爽卑懼，似有求焉。」
value.en: His spirit seemed humble and apprehensive, as though he had something to ask."
value.literal: His spirit was humble and fearful, as if he had some request."

value.zh: 澄對曰：「晉世之亂，嵇紹以身衞主，殞命御側，亦是晉之忠臣；
value.en: Cheng replied, "During the disorders of Jin, Xi Shao shielded his lord with his own body and died at the emperor's side; he was a loyal minister of Jin.
value.literal: Cheng replied, "In the disorder of the Jin age, Xi Shao used his own body to defend his lord and died beside the imperial carriage; he too was a loyal minister of Jin.

value.zh: 比干遭紂兇虐，忠諫剖心，可謂殷之良士。
value.en: Bigan suffered King Zhou's cruelty and had his heart cut out for his loyal remonstrance; he may be called a worthy man of Yin.
value.literal: Bigan met the savagery of Zhou, and because of loyal remonstrance had his heart cut open; he may be called a worthy man of Yin.

value.zh: 二人俱死於王事，墳塋並在於道周。
value.en: Both men died in service to their rulers, and both of their tombs lie beside the road.
value.literal: Both men died in royal service, and their tombs are both beside the road.

value.zh: 然陛下徙御經殷墟而弔比干，至洛陽而遺嵇紹，當是希恩而感夢。」
value.en: Yet as Your Majesty traveled, you passed the ruins of Yin and mourned Bigan, but when you reached Luoyang you passed over Xi Shao. He must have sought your favor and moved you through a dream."
value.literal: Yet when Your Majesty moved the imperial carriage, you passed through the ruins of Yin and mourned Bigan, but reached Luoyang and omitted Xi Shao. It must be that he sought grace and moved you in a dream."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「朕何德，能幽感達士也。
value.en: Gaozu said, "What virtue do I possess, that I could move a worthy man in the unseen world?
value.literal: Gaozu said, "What virtue do I have that I can make a hidden response reach a worthy man?

value.zh: 然實思追禮先賢，標揚忠懿，比干、嵇紹皆是古之誠烈，而朕務濃於比干，禮略於嵇紹，情有愧然。
value.en: Still, I have truly wished to honor former worthies and make loyalty and righteousness shine. Bigan and Xi Shao were both faithful heroes of antiquity, but I gave Bigan rich attention and Xi Shao only slight rites. I am ashamed of this.
value.literal: Yet I truly thought to pursue rites for former worthies and make loyalty and righteousness manifest. Bigan and Xi Shao were both sincere and fierce men of antiquity, but my attention was abundant toward Bigan and my rites slight toward Xi Shao, and in feeling I am ashamed.

value.zh: 既有此夢，或如任城所言。」
value.en: Since this dream has occurred, perhaps it is just as Rencheng says."
value.literal: Since there has been this dream, perhaps it is as Rencheng has said."

value.zh: 於是求其兆域，遣使弔祭焉。
value.en: He then searched for the site of Xi Shao's tomb and sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice there.
value.literal: Thereupon he sought the boundaries of Xi Shao's grave site and sent envoys to offer mourning and sacrifice there.

value.zh: 蕭鸞既殺蕭昭業而自立，昭業雍州刺史曹虎請以襄陽內附。
value.en: After Xiao Luan killed Xiao Zhaoye and took power, Cao Hu, Zhaoye's Inspector of Yongzhou, asked to surrender Xiangyang.
value.literal: After Xiao Luan killed Xiao Zhaoye and set himself up, Cao Hu, Zhaoye's Inspector of Yongzhou, requested to bring Xiangyang in allegiance.

value.zh: 分遣諸將，車駕將自赴之。
value.en: Gaozu sent out several generals and was preparing to go there in person.
value.literal: Gaozu separately dispatched the various generals, and the imperial carriage was about to go there in person.

value.zh: 豫州又表，虎奉誠之使不復重來。
value.en: Yuzhou then reported that no further envoy had come from Hu to confirm his sincerity.
value.literal: Yuzhou further memorialized that Hu's envoy offering sincerity had not come again.

value.zh: 高祖引澄及咸陽王禧、彭城王勰、司徒馮誕、司空穆亮、鎮南李沖等議之。
value.en: Gaozu summoned Cheng, Yuan Xi the Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xie the Prince of Pengcheng, Situ Feng Dan, Sikong Mu Liang, General Who Guards the South Li Chong, and others to discuss the matter.
value.literal: Gaozu brought in Cheng, Xianyang Prince Xi, Pengcheng Prince Xie, Minister over the Masses Feng Dan, Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Guards the South Li Chong, and others to discuss it.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「比得邊州表云，襄陽慕化，朕將鳴鑾江沔，為彼聲勢。
value.en: Gaozu said, "Recently I received a report from the border province saying that Xiangyang longed for our transforming rule, and I was about to take the imperial carriage to the Jiang and Mian to support them.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Recently I received a memorial from the border province saying that Xiangyang admires our transformation, and I was about to sound the imperial bells by the Jiang and Mian to give them support.

value.zh: 今復表稱，更無後信，於行留之計，竟欲如何？」
value.en: Now another report says there has been no later message. So, on the question of going or staying, what do you finally advise?"
value.literal: Now another memorial says that there has been no later message. As for the plan to go or remain, what, in the end, do you intend?"

value.zh: 禧等或云宜行，或言宜止。
value.en: Xi and the others were divided, some saying they should go and others saying they should stop.
value.literal: Xi and the others sometimes said it was fitting to go, and sometimes said it was fitting to stop.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「眾人紛紜，意見不等，朕莫知所從。
value.en: Gaozu said, "Everyone is arguing at once and their opinions differ; I do not know whose advice to follow.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "The many men are in confusion, and their opinions are not the same; I do not know which to follow.

value.zh: 必欲盡行留之勢，使言理俱暢者，宜有客主，共相起發。
value.en: If we are to examine fully the case for going and the case for staying, so that both argument and principle are clear, we should set up opposing sides to draw each other out.
value.literal: If we must exhaust the strengths of going and staying, and have words and principle both fully expressed, there should be guest and host, mutually drawing each other out.

value.zh: 任城與鎮南為應留之議，朕當為宜行之論，諸公俱坐聽得失，長者從之。」
value.en: Rencheng and the General Who Guards the South may argue for staying, and I will argue for going. Let the lords sit and hear the merits of each side, and then follow the better case."
value.literal: Rencheng and General Who Guards the South will make the argument for staying; I shall make the argument for going. Let all the lords sit and listen to the gains and losses, and follow the superior argument."

value.zh: 於是高祖曰：「二賢試言留計也。」
value.en: Gaozu then said, "Let the two worthies state the plan for staying."
value.literal: Thereupon Gaozu said, "Let the two worthies try to speak on the plan for staying."

value.zh: 沖對曰：「臣等正以徒御草創，人斯樂安，內而應者未審，不宜輕爾動發。」
value.en: Li Chong replied, "We only think that the retinue has just been organized, the people are content with peace, and the supposed supporters inside have not been confirmed. We should not set out lightly."
value.literal: Chong replied, "We simply think that the servants and escorts have only just been established, the people are now happy in peace, and those within who would respond have not been verified; it is not fitting to set out lightly."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「襄陽款問，似當是虛。
value.en: Gaozu said, "Xiangyang's offer of submission may well be false.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "The message of submission from Xiangyang seems likely to be false.

value.zh: 亦知初遷之民，無宜勞役。
value.en: I also know that the people newly moved to the capital should not be burdened with service.
value.literal: I also know that the people who have just been moved should not be burdened with labor.

value.zh: 脫歸誠有實，即當乘其悅附，遠則有會稽之會，近則略平江北。
value.en: But if their surrender is genuine, we should take advantage of their willingness to attach themselves to us. At best, we might hold an assembly at Kuaiji; at least, we could bring the land north of the Yangzi roughly under control.
value.literal: But if the return to sincerity is real, then we should take advantage of their pleased attachment; at the farthest there may be an assembly at Kuaiji, and at the nearest we may roughly pacify the north of the Yangzi.

value.zh: 如其送款是虛，且可遊巡淮楚，問民之瘼，使彼土蒼生，知君德之所在，復何所損而惜此一舉？
value.en: If the offer is false, we can still tour Huai and Chu, inquire into the people's hardships, and let the people there see where the ruler's virtue lies. What harm would that do, that we should shrink from this single move?
value.literal: If their sending of submission is false, we can simply make an inspection tour of Huai and Chu, ask after the people's sufferings, and let the common people of that land know where the ruler's virtue lies. What loss would there be, that we should begrudge this one move?

value.zh: 脫降問是實，而停不撫接，不亦稽阻款誠，毀朕大略也。」
value.en: If the surrender is real and we halt without receiving and reassuring them, would that not block their sincere submission and ruin my larger plan?"
value.literal: If the surrender message is real, and we stop without comforting and receiving them, would this not delay and obstruct their sincerity of submission and ruin my grand strategy?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「降問若審，應有表質。
value.en: Cheng said, "If the surrender report were reliable, there should be a formal memorial and pledge.
value.literal: Cheng said, "If the surrender message were verified, there should be a memorial and pledge.

value.zh: 而使人一返，靜無音問，其詐也可見。
value.en: But since the envoy returned, there has been only silence and no further message. Its falseness is obvious.
value.literal: But after the envoy returned once, there has been silence and no further word; its falseness can be seen.

value.zh: 今代遷之眾，人懷戀本，細累相攜，始就洛邑，居無一椽之室，家闕儋石之糧，而使怨苦即戎，泣當白刃，恐非歌舞之師也。
value.en: The people moved from Dai still long for their old home. They have only just reached Luoyang with their families and dependents; they have not even a single-raftered house to live in, and their households lack a bare measure of grain. If we drive them bitterly to war, weeping before drawn blades, this will hardly be an army marching in joy.
value.literal: Now the multitude moved from Dai all cherish attachment to their roots; bringing wives, children, and small dependents, they have only just reached Luoyi, have no house of even a single rafter to live in, and their households lack even a dan or shi of grain. To make them resentfully and bitterly take up arms, weeping before naked blades, I fear this is not an army of song and dance.

value.zh: 今茲區宇初構，又東作方興，正是子來百堵之日，農夫肆力之秋，宜寬彼逋誅，惠此民庶。
value.en: This region is only newly founded, and the spring labors are just beginning. It is the time for the people to build the city walls and for farmers to spend their strength in the fields. We should defer punishment over there and show kindness to the common people here.
value.literal: Now this region has only just been built, and spring plowing is just beginning. This is precisely the day when the people come to build the hundred walls, the season when farmers exert their strength. It is fitting to be lenient toward those there who have escaped punishment and to show favor to these common people.

value.zh: 且三軍已援，無稽赴接。
value.en: Besides, the armies have already been sent in support; there is no need to rush in person to receive an unverified surrender.
value.literal: Moreover, the three armies have already been sent as support; there is no need for an unverified hastening to receive them.

value.zh: 苟其款實，力足納撫，待克平襄沔，然後動駕。
value.en: If the offer is genuine, our forces are sufficient to receive and pacify them. Once Xiangyang and the Mian region have been secured, the emperor can move then.
value.literal: If their submission is genuine, our forces are enough to take them in and pacify them; wait until Xiangyang and the Mian region have been pacified, and only then move the imperial carriage.

value.zh: 今無故勞涉，空為往返，恐挫損天威，更成賊膽，願上覽盤庚始遷之艱難，下矜詩人由庚之至詠，輯寧新邑，惠康億兆。」
value.en: To make this hard journey without cause, only to go and return in vain, would damage imperial majesty and embolden the rebels. I ask Your Majesty to remember the hardships Pan Geng faced when he first moved the capital, and to heed the poet's deepest praise in "You Geng": settle the new city and bring comfort to the people."
value.literal: Now to labor and travel without cause, merely going and returning in vain, I fear will damage the heavenly majesty and instead embolden the rebels. I beg Your Majesty above to consider the hardships when Pan Geng first moved the capital, and below to pity the utmost chant of the poet in "You Geng," to bring peace to the new city and grant ease to the multitudes."

value.zh: 而司空亮以為宜行，公卿皆同之。
value.en: But Sikong Mu Liang thought they should go, and the high ministers all agreed with him.
value.literal: But Minister of Works Liang considered it fitting to go, and the dukes and ministers all agreed with him.

value.zh: 澄謂亮曰：「公在外見旌鉞既張，而有憂色，每聞談論，不願此行，何得對聖顏更如斯之語也。
value.en: Cheng said to Liang, "Outside, when you saw the banners and axes already set out, you looked worried; whenever you discussed it, you did not want this expedition. How can you now say such things before His Majesty?
value.literal: Cheng said to Liang, "When you were outside and saw the banners and axes already arrayed, you had a worried look; whenever I heard you discuss it, you did not wish for this journey. How can you now, before the sacred countenance, speak like this?

value.zh: 面背不同，事涉欺佞，非所謂論道之德，更失國士之體，或有傾側，當由公輩佞臣。」
value.en: To say one thing to a man's face and another behind his back borders on deceitful flattery. That is not the virtue of one who debates principle, and it falls short of the bearing of a statesman. If the state is thrown off balance, it will be because of flatterers like you."
value.literal: If face and back are not the same, the matter borders on deceit and flattery. This is not the virtue called discussing the Way, and further loses the bearing of a man of state. If there is any leaning and overturning, it will be because of flatterers like you."

value.zh: 李沖曰：「任城王可謂忠於社稷，願陛下深察其言。
value.en: Li Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng can truly be called loyal to the state. I hope Your Majesty will weigh his words carefully.
value.literal: Li Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng may be called loyal to the altars of state. I hope Your Majesty will examine his words deeply.

value.zh: 臣等在外，皆憚征行，唯貴與賤，不謀同辭，仰願聖心裁其可否。」
value.en: Outside court, all of us fear the campaign. High and low have not conferred, yet we say the same thing. I beg Your Majesty to decide what is right."
value.literal: When we are outside, all of us dread a campaign. Noble and base alike do not consult one another yet speak the same words. I look up and hope the sacred mind will decide whether it can be done or not."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「任城適以公等從朕，有如此論。
value.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng made that argument just because you gentlemen sided with me.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng just now used the fact that you gentlemen follow me to make such an argument.

value.zh: 不從朕者，何必皆忠而通識安危也。
value.en: Are all who disagree with me necessarily loyal men with a penetrating grasp of danger and security?
value.literal: Must those who do not follow me all be loyal and penetratingly understand safety and danger?

value.zh: 小忠是大忠之賊，無乃似諸？」
value.en: Small loyalty is the enemy of great loyalty. Is this not something like that?"
value.literal: Small loyalty is the thief of great loyalty. Is this not rather like that?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「臣既愚闇，不識大理，所可言者，雖涉小忠，要是竭盡微款，不知大忠者竟何據？」
value.en: Cheng said, "I am foolish and dim and do not understand great principles. What I say may be only small loyalty, but it is the full measure of my poor sincerity. I do not know: what, in the end, is great loyalty based on?"
value.literal: Cheng said, "I am foolish and benighted and do not know the great principle. What I can say may border on small loyalty, but in the end it exhausts my slight sincerity. I do not know, on what does great loyalty finally rest?"

value.zh: 高祖曰：「任城脫居台鼎之任，欲令大忠在己也。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "If Rencheng held the office of an Excellency, he would want great loyalty to belong to himself."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "If Rencheng were to occupy the responsibility of the Excellencies, he would want great loyalty to reside in himself."

value.zh: 澄曰：「臣誠才非台弼，智闕和鼎，脫得濫居公鉉，庶當官而行，不負愚志。」
value.en: Cheng replied, "My talent is not fit to support the highest offices, and my wisdom is not enough to season the cauldron of state. But if I undeservedly held an Excellency's place, I hope I would act according to the office and not betray my poor intentions."
value.literal: Cheng said, "My talent is indeed not that of a support to the Excellencies, and my wisdom lacks what is needed to harmonize the cauldron. If I should undeservedly occupy the handles of an Excellency, I hope I would act according to my office and not betray my foolish intent."

value.zh: 高祖大笑。
value.en: Gaozu burst out laughing.
value.literal: Gaozu laughed loudly.

value.zh: 澄又謂亮曰：「昔汲黯於漢武前面折公孫食脫粟飯，臥布被，云其詐也。
value.en: Cheng then said to Liang, "Long ago, in front of Emperor Wu of Han, Ji An accused Gongsun Hong to his face of eating coarse grain and sleeping under a plain cloth quilt as a fraud.
value.literal: Cheng again said to Liang, "In the past, before Emperor Wu of Han, Ji An confronted Gongsun Hong to his face for eating coarse grain and sleeping under a cloth quilt, saying that it was fraudulent.

value.zh: 于時公孫謙讓下之。
value.en: At the time, Gongsun humbly yielded and put himself below him.
value.literal: At that time Gongsun modestly yielded and placed himself below him.

value.zh: 武帝歎汲黯至忠，公孫長者，二人稱賢。
value.en: Emperor Wu admired Ji An for utmost loyalty and Gongsun for elder virtue, and both men were praised as worthy.
value.literal: Emperor Wu sighed that Ji An was utterly loyal and Gongsun was an elder of virtue, and the two men were both called worthy.

value.zh: 公既道均昔士，願思長者之言。」
value.en: Since your conduct can equal that of men of old, I hope you will remember the elder's example."
value.literal: Since your way is equal to that of the old scholars, I hope you will think on the words of the elder."

value.zh: 高祖笑曰：「任城欲自比汲黯也。
value.en: Gaozu laughed. "Rencheng wants to compare himself to Ji An.
value.literal: Gaozu laughed and said, "Rencheng wishes to compare himself to Ji An.

value.zh: 且所言是公，未知得失所在，何便謝司空也。」
value.en: Besides, your words concerned the Duke, and we do not yet know who is right or wrong. Why rush to apologize to the Minister of Works?"
value.literal: Besides, what was said concerns the Duke, and it is not yet known where gain and loss lie. Why apologize to the Minister of Works so readily?"

value.zh: 駕遂南伐。
value.en: The emperor then went south on campaign.
value.literal: The imperial carriage then went south on campaign.

value.zh: 五等開建，食邑一千戶。
value.en: When the five ranks of nobility were instituted, his fief was set at one thousand households.
value.literal: When the five ranks were established, his fief was one thousand households.

value.zh: 後從征至懸瓠，以篤疾還京。
value.en: Later he accompanied the campaign to Xuanhu, but returned to the capital because of serious illness.
value.literal: Later he followed the campaign as far as Xuanhu, but because of severe illness returned to the capital.

value.zh: 駕餞之汝濆，賦詩而別。
value.en: The emperor saw him off on the bank of the Ru River, composing poems as they parted.
value.literal: The imperial carriage gave him a farewell banquet on the bank of the Ru and composed poems on parting.

value.zh: 車駕還洛，引見王公侍臣於清徽堂。
value.en: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, he received the princes, dukes, and attendant ministers in Qinghui Hall.
value.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, he received the princes, dukes, and attendant ministers in Qinghui Hall.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「此堂成來，未與王公行宴樂之禮。
value.en: Gaozu said, "Since this hall was completed, I have not yet held a proper feast here with the princes and dukes.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Since this hall was completed, I have not yet performed the rites of feasting and music with the princes and dukes.

value.zh: 後東閤廡堂粗復始就，故今與諸賢欲無高而不昇，無小而不入。」
value.en: Now that the eastern pavilion and side halls have roughly been completed, I want to go through them today with you worthies, ascending every height and entering every small place."
value.literal: Afterward the eastern pavilion and side hall were roughly finished, and therefore today, together with the worthies, I wish there to be no high place we do not ascend and no small place we do not enter."

value.zh: 因之流化渠。
value.en: They then went to the Liuhua Canal.
value.literal: They then went to the Liuhua Canal.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「此曲水者亦有其義，取乾道曲成，萬物無滯。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "This winding water has meaning too. It draws on the Way of Qian, which completes things by bending and leaves all things unobstructed."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "This winding water also has its meaning: it takes from the Way of Qian, which bends to complete things and lets the ten thousand things have no obstruction."

value.zh: 次之洗煩池。
value.en: Next they went to the Xifan Pond.
value.literal: Next they went to the Xifan Pond.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「此池中亦有嘉魚。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "There are fine fish in this pond as well."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "There are fine fish in this pond too."

value.zh: 澄曰：「此所謂『魚在在藻，有頒其首』。」
value.en: Cheng said, "This is what the poem means: "The fish are there among the weeds; large are their heads.""
value.literal: Cheng said, "This is what is meant by, "The fish are there among the weeds; large are their heads.""

value.zh: 高祖曰：「且取『王在靈沼，於牣魚躍』。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "Let us instead take the line, "The king is at the Spirit Pond; it is full, and the fish leap.""
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Let us rather take, "The king is in the Spirit Pond; how full it is, and the fish leap.""

value.zh: 次之觀德殿。
value.en: Next they went to the Hall for Observing Virtue.
value.literal: Next they went to the Hall for Observing Virtue.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「射以觀德，故遂命之。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "Archery is used to observe virtue, so I gave it this name."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Through archery one observes virtue, and therefore I named it so."

value.zh: 次之凝閑堂。
value.en: Next they went to the Ningxian Hall.
value.literal: Next they went to the Ningxian Hall.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「名目要有其義，此蓋取夫子閑居之義。
value.en: Gaozu said, "A name must have meaning. This one draws on the idea of the Master at leisure.
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Names and labels must have meaning; this probably takes the meaning of the Master dwelling at leisure.

value.zh: 不可縱奢以忘儉，自安以忘危，故此堂後作茅茨堂。」
value.en: One must not indulge in luxury and forget thrift, or rest in safety and forget danger. That is why I built the Thatched Hall behind it."
value.literal: One must not indulge extravagance and forget frugality, nor settle in safety and forget danger; therefore behind this hall I built the Thatched Hall."

value.zh: 謂李沖曰：「此東曰步元廡，西曰遊凱廡。
value.en: He said to Li Chong, "The eastern gallery is called Buyuan, and the western one Youkai.
value.literal: He said to Li Chong, "This one to the east is called the Buyuan Gallery, and the one to the west is called the Youkai Gallery.

value.zh: 此堂雖無唐堯之君，卿等當無愧於元、凱。」
value.en: Although this hall has no ruler equal to Tang Yao, you gentlemen should not be ashamed before Yuan and Kai."
value.literal: Though this hall has no ruler like Tang Yao, you gentlemen should have no shame before Yuan and Kai."

value.zh: 沖對曰：「臣既遭唐堯之君，不敢辭元、凱之譽。」
value.en: Chong replied, "Since I have encountered a ruler like Tang Yao, I dare not refuse the praise of being Yuan or Kai."
value.literal: Chong replied, "Since I have met a ruler like Tang Yao, I dare not decline the praise of Yuan and Kai."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「光景垂落，朕同宗則有載考之義，卿等將出無遠，何得默爾，不示德音。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "The daylight is fading. For my clansmen there is the duty of continuing the feast into the night, and you gentlemen are about to withdraw though the hour is not far advanced. How can you stay silent and not give us worthy words?"
value.literal: Gaozu said, "The light and shadows are about to fall. For my men of the same clan, there is the meaning of continuing the night gathering; you gentlemen are about to go out and are not far off, so how can you be silent and not show virtuous sounds?"

value.zh: 即命黃門侍郎崔光、郭祚，通直郎邢巒、崔休等賦詩言志。
value.en: He then ordered Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, Palace Attendants of the Yellow Gates, and Xing Luan, Cui Xiu, and others, Gentlemen for Unrestricted Attendance, to compose poems expressing their thoughts.
value.literal: He at once ordered Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, and Gentleman for Unrestricted Attendance Xing Luan, Cui Xiu, and others to compose poems expressing their intentions.

value.zh: 燭至，公卿辭退。
value.en: When the candles were brought in, the dukes and ministers took their leave.
value.literal: When the candles arrived, the dukes and ministers took leave and withdrew.

value.zh: 李沖再拜上千萬歲壽。
value.en: Li Chong bowed twice and offered a long-life toast of countless years.
value.literal: Li Chong bowed twice and offered a toast for ten thousand times ten thousand years.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「卿向以燭至致辭，復獻千萬之壽，朕報卿以南山之詩。」
